newsitem.title: USA: Major stock movements overnight - April 16.
newsitem.headline: Major stock movements overnight - April 16.

text.p: NEW YORK - U.S. blue chips recovered strongly from a mid-afternoon decline as selling pressure on technology stocks appeared to wane. By 8 a.m. NZT the Dow was up 135 points (2.10 percent) at 6,587.

LONDON - UK's leading blue chips ended with solid gains on Tuesday as benign U.S. inflation data sparked a sharp rally on Wall Street and restored investors' confidence, dealers and strategists said. The benchmark FTSE 100 index closed 35.1 points higher at 4,286.8, as advancers broadly outpaced decliners 78 to 16.

FRANKFURT - German shares on Tuesday closed at higher levels reached earlier after Wall Street's overnight gains, but were unable to build on that firmness as caution ahead of U.S. consumer price data due later set in. Dealers said the German market was above all concerned that the figures would show inflationary pressure that could in turn heighten the outlook for a further rise in U.S. interest rates. The 30-share DAX index ended up 47.78 points at 3,327.68 points. In post-bourse trade the index rose 71.74 to 3,369.26.

PARIS - French shares closed 2.12 percent higher on Tuesday, in an upward swing capping a recent series of wild movements, following a volatile Wall Street and underpinned by a firmer dollar. Wall Street's early gains after a favourable March U.S. CPI figure extended Paris' early gains. Traders said the market's direction on Wednesday would be influenced by the March industrial production figure out that day. The CAC-40 closed up 54.50 points at 2,620.63.

ZURICH - Swiss shares gained more than one percent on Tuesday as better-than-expected U.S. price data and Wall Street's firm opening pushed prices higher, dealers said. The Broad SPI closed up 28.84 to 2,935.72.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed moderately higher on Tuesday, supported by a rally in blue-chip issues which was prompted by the Dow industrials' rebound overnight, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average climbed 241.12 points to finish at 17,933.59.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed firmer but well off highs on Tuesday, dragged back by weakness in propety stocks despite sharp gains on Wall Street overnight and continued buying interest in red chips, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index ended 46.05 points higher at 12,342.02.

SYDNEY - Australian shares chalked up respectable gains on Tuesday in response to a rebound on Wall Street after Friday's inflation fear-inspired selloff. However, volumes remained subdued and brokers said the scarcity of investor interest ahead of further U.S. inflation figures had perhaps exaggerated some of the gains made. The All Ordinaries index climbed 15.6 points

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares powered ahead to finish Tuesday on a high following a better-than-expected U.S. CPI number and were further propelled by an early jump on Wall Street. Dealers said that shares had been treading water awaiting the release of the U.S. data which would remove uncertainty from Wall Street and other markets.
